kpis.sub: ALBEMARLE'S CHILE WORKERS VOTE TO STRIKE (SEP 2)
kpis.label: 466 of 478 eligible workers at Albemarle's Chile lithium operations backed a walkout over wage talks; the strike is set to begin 8am local time Sep 7 if negotiations fail, putting a slice of 2026's 70,700t LCE Atacama guidance at risk just as new CEO Ragnar Udd is set to succeed Kent Masters (effective Feb 1, 2027)

kpis.sub: XI'S WASHINGTON VISIT KEEPS RARE-EARTH ACCESS ON THE AGENDA
kpis.label: Reuters reported Sep 4 that a handful of Chinese suppliers have refused to ship rare earths to US buyers since early August, wary of Beijing penalties for complying with the Responsible Minerals Initiative's due-diligence framework. Yttrium exports to the US remain at roughly half 2024 levels; the issue is now on Washington's agenda ahead of Xi's Sep 24 visit, with the Nov 10 export-license and Nov 27 Busan-truce deadlines still unresolved

kpis.sub: USA RARE EARTH COMPLETES SERRA VERDE COMBINATION (SEP 3)
kpis.label: Deal formally closed — $300M cash plus 126,849,307 new shares — with legacy USAR/Serra Verde holders owning ~66%/34% of the combined company. Thras Moraitis becomes President immediately (CEO effective Oct 1); Sir Mick Davis joins the board. Stock has settled to ~$17.61, well off its 52-week high of $43.98

kpis.sub: FREEPORT CUTS 2026 COPPER GUIDANCE ON GRASBERG DELAY
kpis.label: FY2026 copper output guidance cut to 3.1B lbs from 3.4B lbs (gold cut to 650k oz from 800k oz) on a delayed ramp-up needing ore-loading infrastructure modifications. Stock still near $72-73 (market cap past $100B) on an Indonesia life-of-resource extension agreement; copper itself holds near $6.52-6.60/lb, +47.6% YoY

themes.title: Chinese suppliers quietly halt shipments ahead of Xi's visit
themes.description: Reuters reported Sep 4 that a handful of Chinese rare-earth suppliers have refused to ship to US buyers since early August, wary of Beijing penalties for complying with the Responsible Minerals Initiative's due-diligence framework. Yttrium exports to the US remain at roughly half their 2024 level. The issue is now formally on Washington's agenda ahead of Xi Jinping's Sep 24 Washington visit.

themes.title: Three clocks now running — Sep 24, Nov 10, Nov 27
themes.description: Xi's Sep 24 Washington visit is the nearest checkpoint, with rare-earth access explicitly on the agenda; Treasury Secretary Bessent has said the US expects Beijing to fully meet its rare-earth commitments. Behind it sit two truce deadlines — general rare-earth/battery-material export licenses run through roughly Nov 10, 2026, and the Busan truce's gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard pause runs through Nov 27, 2026 — while China's own exit-entry rules tighten from Sep 15 to curb outbound knowhow.

themes.title: Onshoring goes from financing to combining
themes.description: USA Rare Earth's Sep 3 close of its $2.8B Serra Verde combination is the clearest sign yet that Project Vault-era onshoring policy (a $10B EXIM loan plus $2B private capital, backing a 60-mineral strategic reserve) is translating into actual corporate consolidation, not just government financing announcements. The combined USAR-Serra Verde entity becomes one of the only fully integrated rare-earth-to-magnet platforms outside Asia, with Serra Verde bringing scaled heavy-rare-earth production USAR lacked on its own.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + $400M DoD convertible preferred (DoD now largest shareholder, ~15%)
rows.watch for: Shares have eased to ~$54-55 ($9.7B market cap) from the ~$60 August peak; CFO Ryan Corbett presents at the Jefferies Industrials Conference Sep 9, the next scheduled catalyst. The August gadolinium offtake with a US aerospace/defense customer and the "Project Swarm" drone-magnet initiative extend the growth story. DoD's 10X plant (2028) still carries the ≥$140M EBITDA guarantee at a $110/kg NdPr floor. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: Confirmed Sep 1-2 that it held (unconsummated) takeover talks earlier this year — "a high level of uncertainty" meant discussions didn't proceed — while the CEO search continues under interim chief Pol Le Roux following Amanda Lacaze's retirement. Shares sit at A$16.26, below both the 50- and 200-day moving averages; leadership overhang is now the live story, layered on top of the FY26 capex-overrun narrative

Chile workers voted 97.49% (466/478) to strike over wage talks, with a walkout set to begin Sep 7 if negotiations fail — a concrete near-term threat to the 70,700t 2026 LCE guidance. New CEO Ragnar Udd succeeds Kent Masters effective Feb 1, 2027, adding a leadership transition on top of the labor risk. Stock at $137.34, down 6.9% YTD vs. the S&P's +13.3%

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: Cut FY2026 guidance — copper to 3.1B lbs from 3.4B lbs, gold to 650k oz from 800k oz — on a delayed Grasberg ramp-up needing ore-loading infrastructure work. Stock still near $72-73 (market cap past $100B) on a life-of-resource extension agreement with Indonesia; copper itself holds near $6.52-6.60/lb, +47.6% YoY, on the Congo export ban and weak Chile/Peru output. Lutnick's overdue Section 232 refined-copper tariff decision remains the next real policy catalyst

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026, priced $17.17)
rows.watch for: The $2.8B Serra Verde combination formally closed Sep 3 — $300M cash plus 126,849,307 new shares, with legacy USAR/Serra Verde holders owning ~66%/34% of the combined company. Thras Moraitis is now President (CEO effective Oct 1) and Sir Mick Davis has joined the board. Stock has settled to ~$17.61 ($4.4B market cap), well off its 52-week high of $43.98, as the dilution digests; integration execution is next to watch

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: Increasingly pivoting toward rare earths — management expects the REE value chain to supply most earnings within five years. Up to $725M in conditional US government support now targets White Mesa's separation expansion and downstream magnet capacity; pilot output has reached ~29kg of 99.9%-purity Dy oxide, ahead of the 99.5% automotive spec. Stock ~$14.50 (Sep 4); the $1.9B VAC deal still targets an early-2027 close

No major new catalyst this week — bicarbonate reactors for the lithium-carbonate crystallization plant are now under construction, with mechanical completion still targeted late 2027 toward 40,000t/y of battery-grade capacity. The Aug Yorkville convertible facility (up to $175M) sits atop the $2.23B DOE loan for near-term liquidity

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: China lithium carbonate spot sits around $23,161/t (Sep 3, +37% YTD) — up sharply on the year but essentially range-bound recently, with 2026 full-year forecasts revised up even as analysts expect H2 softening. A possible delay to CATL's Jianxiawo mine restart complicates the simple oversupply story. Copper has held up better (+47.6% YoY) but is still down slightly over the trailing month — a reminder that both metals can swing on a single mine or regulatory decision.

bear_case.title: China can flood the market — or freeze the tap
bear_case.description: The same country whose restarted mines feed lithium-glut fears is, per Reuters' Sep 4 reporting, also the one whose suppliers are voluntarily halting US rare-earth shipments over fear of Beijing sanctions tied to the Responsible Minerals Initiative. Investors betting on either a supply glut or a supply squeeze are making a bet on Beijing's posture, not just on markets.

bear_case.title: Execution and leadership risk across the board
bear_case.description: This week hit nearly every name at once: Freeport cut its FY2026 copper and gold guidance on a Grasberg ramp-up delay; Albemarle's Chile workforce voted 97.49% to strike just as a new, not-yet-seated CEO was named; and Lynas confirmed failed takeover talks while its CEO search stretches past five months. USA Rare Earth absorbed 126.85M new shares of dilution to close Serra Verde. Even the sector's most established and most consolidated names are working through operational or leadership disruption, not operating from settled strength.

bear_case.title: Policy dependency, now with a hard date
bear_case.description: Xi Jinping's Sep 24 Washington visit adds a specific near-term date to a policy dependency that was previously open-ended: rare-earth licensing frictions, the Busan truce's two separate November expirations, and Lutnick's still-overdue Section 232 refined-copper tariff decision (a proposal would phase in a 15% tariff from 2027, rising to 30% by 2028) are all live simultaneously. A visit that resolves the shipment halts would be bullish; one that doesn't leaves the sector exposed into year-end.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Only fully integrated US rare-earth producer with DoD as top shareholder; the pullback to $54-55 from the ~$60 August peak looks like normal digestion rather than a thesis break, and CFO Ryan Corbett's Sep 9 Jefferies appearance is the next catalyst. Weight raised modestly to absorb capital freed by moving Albemarle to Watch. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: Confirmed Sep 1-2 it held takeover talks earlier this year that ultimately didn't proceed, removing an M&A catalyst just as the CEO search under interim chief Pol Le Roux stretches past five months. Record FY26 revenue doesn't offset an unresolved leadership vacuum layered on the Malaysia capex overrun.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Moved to Watch: Chile workers voted 97.49% (466 of 478) to strike, with a walkout set to begin Sep 7 if wage talks fail, threatening a slice of the 70,700t 2026 LCE Atacama guidance just as a new, unproven CEO (Ragnar Udd, effective Feb 1, 2027) is named. Good lithium business, but this week adds a concrete near-term operating disruption on top of a leadership handoff — exactly the 'wrong point in the cycle' case for Watch.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Cut FY2026 guidance — copper to 3.1B lbs from 3.4B lbs, gold to 650k oz from 800k oz — on a delayed Grasberg ramp-up, but the stock has held near $72-73 (market cap past $100B) on a life-of-resource extension agreement with Indonesia and copper still +47.6% YoY. Staying Core on the copper macro and the Indonesia resolution, but the guidance miss is now the thing to track.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: The $2.8B Serra Verde combination formally closed Sep 3 — $300M cash plus 126,849,307 new shares — resolving the deal-completion uncertainty that justified caution before. Stock has settled to ~$17.61, well off its post-listing highs as the dilution digests; weight raised modestly but integration execution keeps this speculative.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: Up to $725M in conditional US government support now targets White Mesa's separation expansion and downstream magnet capacity, and pilot output has hit 29kg of 99.9%-purity Dy oxide — ahead of the 99.5% automotive spec. Weight raised on that progress, but the VAC deal still needs an early-2027 close and White Mesa's uranium side remains paused.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: No new catalyst this week — construction on Thacker Pass's lithium-carbonate crystallization plant continues (bicarbonate reactors now underway) toward late-2027 mechanical completion. Weight held at the sector's smallest speculative size pending a fresh catalyst.
